newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ sees imminent PNG/Bougainville peace talks.
newsitem.headline: NZ sees imminent PNG/Bougainville peace talks.

text.p: New Zealand's Foreign Affairs Minister Don McKinnon was due to announce on Wednesday that talks were "imminent" in New Zealand between parties to the long-running secessionist rebellion on Bougainville Island, Papua New Guinea.
Mackinnon said he planned a news conference at 0030 GMT at which he would make a statement on "imminent talks between Bougainville groups in New Zealand".

In the statement McKinnon said the meeting would bring together senior members of the Bougainville transitional government, the Bougainville interim government and the Bougainville Revolutionary Army (BRA). The talks were due to begin at an army camp near the South Island city of Christchurch this weekend, he added.

"This is a step along the path towards settlement of their differences with the Papua New Guinea Government. It should not be assumed there is a quick fix solution to the situation in Bougainville," he said in the statement.
The conflict on the resource-rich island, 800 kilometres (500 miles) northeast of Port Moresby, has claimed thousands of lives and dates back more than eight years.

In March, PNG was plunged into its worst political crisis since independence when the army revolted over Prime Minister Sir Julius Chan's hiring of mercenaries to end the Bougainville rebellion. Chan lost his seat in nationalist elections on Tuesday, and predicted his career in politics was over. He said the US$36 million mercenary plan had been to blame for his downfall.
